_note: Hand-reviewed prompt pack for the English definition and expression prompts.
Mined from the 2025 corpus (13,518 definition cells, 5,989 expression cells)
by the same method as the Chinese pack; the measured basis for every value is
recorded in observations/v3-patch-crew-C.md.
English is the recorded special case: the frozen V4 core has no CRITICAL RULE
block for it, and the script contract is nearly vacuous (Latin only).
The one real English defect the corpus shows is not a script defect at all:
the capital-plus-full-stop register holds in only 80.2% of cells, and the
split does not follow part of speech, so it is generation noise. The pack
pins the majority form.
COVERAGE METHOD for fixed_renderings_table: each percentage is the share of
definition cells whose DANISH definition contains the left-hand formula (for
the frame rows, the `der` form: `person der`, `noget der`) and whose target
gloss contains the right-hand rendering. Stated because a reviewer read the
`der/som` label as the denominator and could not land on the value: the
`der|som` denominator gives 60.0 / 36.5 / 58.9% for noget and 76.5 / 81.1 /
73.2% for person (EN/DE/ES), i.e. the whole table would shift, not one row.
Re-derived 2026-08-26: the `der`-form numbers reproduce exactly.
Danish text in the worked examples is HAND-AUTHORED in DDO's editorial style.
No DDO source text is stored in this file.
allowed_scripts: Latin letters, ASCII punctuation, and Arabic digits
orthography_rules: Begin the `gloss` with a capital letter and end it with a single full stop (80.2% of shipped cells do exactly this; the remaining 19.2% are generation noise, not a second register, because the split does not follow part of speech). Keep the `lemma` lowercase unless it is a proper name (98.6%).
lemma_charset_rule: Latin letters, spaces, and hyphens. No digits, no quotation marks, no phonetic transcription.
punctuation_rule: ASCII punctuation only. Commas are normal (43.5% of glosses); a semicolon may carry a short synonym tail (14.0%). Colons, slashes and quotation marks are effectively absent (under 0.3% each); do not introduce them.
pos_vb: Give the bare verb, never with `to` (94.0% of shipped verb lemmas are bare). The `to` lives at the start of the gloss instead (95.0% of verb glosses).
pos_sb: Give the bare singular noun with no article (0.55% of lemmas break this). The `gloss` normally opens with `a` or `the` (79.1%).
pos_function: Open the `gloss` with `Used` and name the function: 35.9% of function-word glosses and 87.0% of interjection glosses do this.

definitions.gloss: The act of moving something towards oneself using force.
A current of cold air moving through a room, for example from an open door.
A characteristic quality of a person or thing, often one that is easy to identify.

fixed_renderings_table: om person       -> about a person / of a person
med hensyn til  -> with regard to (40.0%)
anti_patterns: bad lemma to pull -> the infinitive marker belongs at the start of the gloss, not in the lemma (1.86% of shipped lemmas carry it) -> good lemma pull
bad lemma noun suffix -> a grammatical label instead of a concept (V4 lemma rule 2) -> good: name the meaning the element contributes
bad gloss a current of cold air moving through a room -> no capital and no full stop, against a capital-to-full-stop register -> good gloss A current of cold air moving through a room.

bad gloss The act of moving something towards oneself using force, which physicists call tension. -> over-explaining past the Danish definition (V4 gloss rule 2) -> good gloss The act of moving something towards oneself using force.
length_targets: lemma: one word is the norm (65.7% of cells), two words 26.1%, three 6.8%. Median 8 characters, 90th percentile 15.
gloss: 11 words is the median, 21 the 90th percentile, 34 the 99th; above 25 words needs a reason. Exactly one sentence, capital letter to a single full stop.
gloss_allowed_set: Latin letters, ASCII punctuation, Arabic digits, and the Danish letters æ ø å when a Danish word or letter is named

fixed_expressions.gloss: To be strong-willed and willing to assert oneself.
To become wildly excited or to lose control completely.
